OSKAR
Senior Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer

[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [PORTFOLIO OR GITHUB]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications. Strongest in frontend development with React and TypeScript, with professional experience delivering backend services using Node.js, NestJS and PostgreSQL. Recent work includes patient onboarding identity verification, secure document upload and an incremental backend migration. Experienced as a project tech lead and, in 2024, acting team lead for four months.

CORE SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, Angular, React Native
Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express, Laravel, Apollo Server
Databases and data: PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma
Cloud and messaging: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS; Firebase Cloud Messaging
Other: WordPress, GraphQL (maintained an Apollo Server BFF), Python (basic), YAML

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Full-Stack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB
2021–Present
- Develop onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL, with AWS services.
- Built a BankID identity verification step supporting QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK. A/B tested on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Delivered a secure document-upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, and SQS scan-status updates into PostgreSQL.
- Contributed to an incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, moving route by route behind the same API gateway.
- Maintained an Apollo Server BFF.
- Acted as team lead for four months in 2024 during the lead’s parental leave, including 1:1s and sprint planning.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB
2018–2021
- Delivered client web and mobile projects using Angular, React, React Native, Laravel and WordPress.
- Served as project tech lead and built most of a React Native ferry-ticket app in a two-developer team. The app supports ticket purchase and offline ticket display and has approximately 50,000 downloads.

Developer | Nordkust Media
2014–2018
- Worked on newspaper websites.

SELECTED PROJECTS

BankID Identity Verification Flow | Älvgrind Fintech, 2022
- Built a new onboarding identity-verification step using Swedish BankID, with QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK.
- A/B tested with 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS.

Secure Document Upload | Älvgrind Fintech, 2023
- Implemented customer ID-document uploads (up to 20 MB) using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning in Lambda, and scan-status handling through SQS into PostgreSQL.
- Technologies: AWS S3, Lambda, SQS, NestJS, PostgreSQL.

Express to NestJS Migration | Älvgrind Fintech, 2021–2022
- Contributed to an incremental onboarding-backend migration, moving routes from Express to NestJS behind the same API gateway.
- Gave a meetup talk about the migration in 2022.
- Technologies: Node.js, Express, NestJS, TypeORM, Prisma.

Ferry Ticket Mobile App | Sjöbris Digital, 2019–2020
- Tech lead in a two-developer team; built most of a React Native app for buying and showing ferry tickets offline. The app has approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Technologies: React Native, TypeScript, Node.js, Firebase Cloud Messaging.

Home Assistant Integrations | Personal project, 2022–Present
- Built two small custom home-automation integrations, published on GitHub with approximately 40 stars combined.
- Technologies: Python (basic), YAML.

LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCE
Acting Team Lead | Älvgrind Fintech, 2024
- Covered the team lead role for four months during parental leave, handling 1:1s and sprint planning.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured senior engineering CV with clear progression, credible technical breadth, and several quantified outcomes. The BankID conversion result, secure upload implementation, migration work, meetup talk, team-lead coverage, and 50,000-download mobile app provide useful evidence of impact. The document is concise and professionally written. The main content issues are incomplete contact details, some repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Projects, and one misleading description that refers to fintech onboarding as patient onboarding. The CV also does not document several requirements that are important for this role, particularly automated testing, Git workflows, accessibility, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, and explicit security knowledge.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, chronological experience, readable bullets, and conventional technology names such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, Express, and GraphQL. There are no apparent tables, graphics, columns, icons, or unusual formatting that would impair parsing. AI/ATS screening probability is high for the core React/TypeScript/Node.js/PostgreSQL/AWS profile and moderate overall for this particular vacancy because several must-have keywords are absent: automated testing, unit testing, end-to-end testing, Git, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, authentication, and OWASP Top 10. The contact placeholders could also reduce practical usability even though they do not usually affect keyword parsing. Repeated project content is acceptable but uses space that could otherwise strengthen requirement coverage.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the central technical stack: it shows substantially more than two years of professional React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, SQL/PostgreSQL, NestJS, AWS, analytics/A/B testing, and experience handling identity verification and customer ID documents. The secure upload project provides relevant evidence of security-conscious engineering, although it does not establish explicit authentication or OWASP Top 10 knowledge. The candidate's fintech background is relevant to regulated, sensitive-data work, but the CV does not show healthcare experience or GDPR/health-data privacy work. The document also does not show semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, automated unit or end-to-end testing, Git workflows, Docker, Next.js/SSR, Storybook/design systems, German, or Croatian. English is demonstrated by the fluent English CV, though fluency is not explicitly stated. The leadership and project-tech-lead experience supports the role's collaborative, low-ego, mentoring-oriented environment, but mentoring interns or junior colleagues is not evidenced.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, change “Recent work includes patient onboarding identity verification” to “Recent work includes fintech customer onboarding identity verification” or “Recent work includes identity verification for fintech onboarding.” The source material describes fintech/customer onboarding, not patient onboarding; the current wording could inaccurately imply healthcare experience.

CRITICAL — In the header, replace “[EMAIL]”, “[PHONE]”, “[LINKEDIN]”, and “[PORTFOLIO OR GITHUB]” with the candidate’s actual contact details and links. Do not invent or infer any details; use only real information supplied by the candidate. If a link is not available, remove that placeholder rather than leaving bracketed text.

MINOR — In the Professional Experience section, reduce duplication with Selected Projects. Keep the quantified outcomes and implementation details in the relevant employment bullets, and shorten the corresponding project entries to one or two lines each, or retain Selected Projects only for work that adds material detail not already present under employment. This will improve scanability without removing evidence.

MINOR — In the Full-Stack Developer role at Älvgrind Fintech AB, change “Develop onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL, with AWS services” to the more ATS-specific “Develop fintech customer-onboarding features with React and TypeScript, and backend services with NestJS and PostgreSQL on AWS.” This uses the job description’s terminology while remaining supported by the candidate information.
critique.critical_issues:
1. Potential factual misrepresentation: the Professional Summary describes “patient onboarding identity verification,” but the original candidate information describes fintech onboarding and customer ID verification, not patient onboarding. Fix: replace “patient onboarding” with “fintech customer onboarding” or equivalent accurate wording.
2. Incomplete application header: the CV contains unresolved placeholders for email, phone, LinkedIn, and portfolio/GitHub. Fix: replace them with the candidate’s actual details or remove unavailable fields.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear senior full-stack/frontend positioning, quantified achievements, relevant technologies, and credible leadership evidence. The BankID conversion improvement, 50,000-download mobile app, secure document-upload implementation, and incremental migration are especially persuasive. The content is professional and generally concise. The main content limitation is that several job-relevant areas—automated testing, Git workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, and explicit security terminology—are not covered. These are not necessarily candidate deficiencies; most are simply unsupported by the supplied candidate information. There is also some repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Projects, although the project section adds useful detail.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly headings, standard employment formatting, plain text technology names, and strong searchable terms including React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, Express, GraphQL, S3, Lambda, SQS, and A/B testing. The AI screening probability is good, approximately 80–85%, because the core stack and relevant fintech/security work are explicit. Screening may be weaker for this particular advert because the CV does not contain supported evidence or terminology for automated testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, OWASP Top 10, Docker, or English proficiency. Do not add unsupported technologies or practices merely to match the advert. The CV would benefit from making existing security and experimentation experience more directly searchable and from reducing duplicated project descriptions.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the core full-stack stack: it clearly shows substantially more than two years of professional React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, and A/B testing. The fintech onboarding and identity-verification work is relevant to Verdane Care's emphasis on privacy, responsible handling of sensitive data, and secure patient-facing workflows. The candidate also demonstrates technical leadership, sprint planning, and 1:1 experience, which supports the small-squad environment. However, the supplied material does not establish experience with semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, automated testing, Git-based workflows, Docker, healthcare/privacy requirements, German/Croatian, or SSR frameworks. Fintech identity verification and secure document handling provide relevant security and regulated-environment evidence, but they should not be represented as healthcare or GDPR experience. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. No unsupported claims or apparent hallucinations were detected in the CV when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR / HIGH-IMPACT IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Core Skills section, add a separate line such as “Security and experimentation: BankID authentication, secure file uploads, S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning, A/B testing” using only the technologies and activities already documented in the experience and project sections. This will make the CV’s strongest relevance to “web security fundamentals” and “analytics and A/B testing” more visible to ATS screening.
2. In the Full-Stack Developer section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, revise the first bullet to use the advert’s exact supported terminology: “Build patient-relevant transferable experience in fintech customer-onboarding features with React and TypeScript, plus Node.js/NestJS backend services and PostgreSQL on AWS.” Do not call the work healthcare or patient-facing, since the supplied evidence is fintech rather than healthcare.
3. In the BankID Identity Verification Flow project, change “Built a QR-code and same-device onboarding identity-verification step” to “Built a QR-code and same-device identity-verification flow using a provider SDK; A/B tested on 10% of traffic before rollout, increasing onboarding conversion from 61% to 74%.” This places authentication, SDK integration, experimentation, and measurable impact in one ATS-readable bullet.
4. In the Secure Document Upload project, retain the existing technical detail but make the security relevance explicit without overstating it: “Implemented secure ID-document uploads with S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV malware scanning in Lambda, and SQS scan-status updates into PostgreSQL.”
5. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects by keeping the concise outcome-focused bullets in Professional Experience and using Selected Projects for the deeper implementation details. In particular, avoid repeating the full BankID conversion figures and the full ferry-app description twice; retain each metric once in the most prominent location and use the other section for complementary technical context.
6. In the Home Assistant Integrations project, retain the GitHub publication and approximately 40 stars because they are supported evidence of public project work, but do not label this as professional Python experience or use it as evidence of Git-based professional workflows.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, and presents a strong core profile for a TypeScript/React full-stack role. The strongest evidence is concrete and quantified: 12 years of experience, React/TypeScript, Node.js/NestJS, PostgreSQL, BankID, secure uploads, AWS, a 61% to 74% conversion improvement, and a mobile app with approximately 50,000 downloads. The selected-projects section is particularly persuasive. However, the opening bullet under Älvgrind contains awkward and unclear wording ('Build patient-relevant transferable experience'), and the CV repeats several project details across Professional Experience and Selected Projects. The document also lacks standard contact/header information as provided, which reduces practical usability.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, standard job titles, dates, and technology keywords are ATS-friendly. It should score well for React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, GraphQL, React Native, authentication, secure file uploads, and A/B testing. AI screening probability is medium-high for the core full-stack requirements, but lower for this specific vacancy because the CV does not show semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, automated testing, Git workflows, Docker, or health-data privacy. These should not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience. The lack of contact details and the duplicated project content are also practical ATS/recruiter weaknesses. Use a standard header with actual contact details, LinkedIn, GitHub, and portfolio links where available; do not invent or add unsupported information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the core technical scope: the candidate clearly exceeds the React/TypeScript experience requirement and demonstrates Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, AWS, authentication, secure document handling, and A/B testing. The fintech onboarding work is relevant to a regulated environment and supports the employer's 'Privacy by default' emphasis, although it is not healthcare experience. The candidate also shows ownership, technical leadership, sprint planning, and measurable user-impact work, which fit a small, user-focused squad. The main alignment limitations are that the supplied material does not evidence semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, automated unit/integration/end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, Docker, design systems, Storybook, German/Croatian, or explicit willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be solved by unsupported CV claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the Professional Experience section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, replace the bullet 'Build patient-relevant transferable experience in fintech customer-onboarding features with React and TypeScript, plus Node.js/NestJS backend services and PostgreSQL on AWS.' This wording is grammatically incorrect and 'patient-relevant' is not supported by the candidate information. Use: 'Build fintech customer-onboarding features with React and TypeScript, plus Node.js/NestJS backend services and PostgreSQL on AWS.'

2. At the top of the CV, directly below 'OSKAR', add the candidate's actual phone number, email address, professional location, and relevant LinkedIn/GitHub/portfolio URLs if available. Do not use placeholders or invent details.

MINOR / HIGH-VALUE:
3. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. Keep the detailed metrics and implementation details in Selected Projects, and shorten the corresponding experience bullets. For example, under Älvgrind Fintech retain the scope, technologies, leadership, and one-line outcomes, while leaving the full BankID, document-upload, and migration descriptions in Selected Projects.

4. In the Professional Summary, make the job-relevant positioning more direct by changing the opening to: 'Full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications, strongest in frontend development with React and TypeScript and experienced in Node.js/NestJS backend services with PostgreSQL.' Retain the BankID, secure-upload, migration, and technical-lead evidence afterward.

5. In the Core Skills section, change 'Security and experimentation' to 'Security, authentication and experimentation' so the existing BankID authentication and secure-upload experience is easier for ATS and recruiters to identify. Do not add OWASP, GDPR, accessibility, testing, Git, Docker, or health-data terms unless the candidate can substantiate them.

6. Under Leadership Experience, avoid repeating the same acting-team-lead information already present under Älvgrind. Either remove the separate Leadership Experience section or shorten the experience bullet to: 'Acting team lead for four months in 2024 during parental leave, handling 1:1s and sprint planning.' Keep the fuller version in only one location.

7. In the Ferry Ticket Mobile App project, preserve the useful ownership clarification but make the impact easier to scan: 'Project tech lead in a two-developer team; built most of the React Native app. Supports ticket purchase and offline ticket display; approximately 50,000 downloads.'

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused CV with a clear Full-Stack Engineer positioning and credible evidence of React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, fintech onboarding, identity verification, secure document handling, migration work, and technical leadership.
